sections.heading: How to Play Balance
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Balance"]Balance Druid Rotation in Midnight[/h2]
[pad]

Balance Druid is fairly straightforward if you understand a few fundamentals of the spec itself. Everything else just falls into place nicely with talents and Hero Talents. The core concepts to keep in mind are these, in order of importance:

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange size=medium type=round color=c11 inline=true][/icon][/td]
[td][b][color=c11]Eclipse usage:[/color][/b] [spell=1239669] is a 32 second cooldown, letting you enter either [spell=1233346] or [spell=1233272] depending on your previously cast builder. Casting [spell=5176] makes the button enter [spell=1233346] and casting [spell=194153] makes the button enter [spell=1233272]. Optimizing time inside [spell=1239669] is important to your damage as a [color=c11]Balance Druid[/color], and you want to overlap this effect with other short cooldowns like [spell=205636] if you're playing [color=necrolord]Keeper of the Grove[/color]  or [spell=202770] if you're playing [color=c9]Elune's Chosen.[/color][/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_mage_firestarter size=medium type=round color=c11 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c11]Spread DoTs:[/color][/b] Our DoT effects in [spell=8921] and [spell=93402] provide a substantial damage gain due to the number of ticks from your [color=unfriendly]DoTs[/color] interacting with [spell=202342]. During Mythic+ encounters, you should start a pull spreading [spell=8921] on as many targets as possible, prioritizing the mobs with the most HP. After the mobs are sufficiently stacked, you slam a [spell=93402] so it affects everything and then continue into your cooldown windows.[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=spell_arcane_arcane03 size=medium type=round color=c11 inline=true][/icon][/td]
[td][b][color=c11]Always Be Casting:[/color][/b] Arguably the most important part of playing any caster is to Always Be Casting. Balance Druid's spenders [spell=78674] and [spell=191034] are instant casts which make them very useful when dealing with mechanics that force movement.  What separates an average Balance Druid from a great one is recognizing the moments where you can stand still and build up [resource=8] in order to have spare casts of your spenders. [spell=102401] is also very good for helping with movement.[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian type=round size=medium inline=true][/icon] Balance Druid Major Cooldowns[/h2]

Balance has access to a variety of different cooldowns on its spec tree. All of them come with some extra wrinkles in how they work rather than simply being flat increases, so the section below covers [i]how[/i] they work, and most importantly, how to get the most out of each use.

[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]

[tab name="Eclipse Windows" icon=ability_druid_eclipseorange]

The fundamental in how you approach pressing [spell=1239669] comes down to if you can align it with [spell=205636] or [spell=202770], depending on your chosen hero talent tree. You want to press your cooldowns together whenever applicable, but since [color=c11]Eclipse[/color] and [spell=194223]/[spell=102560] are virtually the same cooldown and the effects overwrite each other, there are things worth keeping in mind whenever you approach a new fight.
	[ul]
	
[li]The [b]Midnight Season 2[/b] tier set buff [spell=1301768] amplifies one of the essential parts in the [color=c11]Balance Druid's[/color] rotation; pooling [resource=8] and preparing for your [color=c11]Eclipse[/color] windows. Spending [color=c11]Astral Power[/color] at the end of your [color=c11]Eclipse[/color] can potentially be a very minor gain, but you also want to consider having [spell=78674] available for movement. [/li]
[li]You should treat [color=c11]Eclipse[/color] as a damage cooldown and apply the standard rules you would on any other damage cooldown. This means to press it with as much resource available as possible while not overcapping the cooldown, and trying to pair it together with your other cooldowns.[/li]
[li]The same logic also applies with what spells you want to cast [b]inside[/b] your [color=c11]Eclipse[/color]. Spells like [color=necrolord]Force of Nature[/color], [spell=93402], [spell=8921] and [color=mage]Fury of Elune[/color] do not really provide any upfront damage by themselves, so you want to avoid using globals on these inside of your biggest cooldown windows, with the exception of whenever you play [color=mage]Fury of Elune[/color] with the [spell=429539] talent where you would just send it off cd and plan your other cooldown windows around it.[/li]
[li]Entering any [color=c11]Eclipse[/color] or pressing [color=mage]Celestial Alignment/Incarnation[/color] resets your current [spell=343647] to 6 seconds no matter what your previous duration was. [/li]
[li]Members of the Dreamgrove discord [url=https://www.dreamgrove.gg/planner]developed this cooldown planner tool[/url] including the many CDR options in the [color=c11]Balance Druid[/color] tree. This tool can be pretty handy if you are interested in seeing how they interact with each other or want to plan cooldowns for an upcoming boss.[/li]
[/ul]

Below is a timeline [b]example[/b] of what a regular [color=c11]Balance Druid[/color] cooldown cadence would be over a 4 minute encounter.
[div]
[wrapper]
[rotation-timeline]
[rt-step=1233272 text="0:01"]
[rt-step-group=102560 text="0:04"]
[rt-sup=202770]
[/rt-step-group]
[rt-step=1233272 text="0:24"]
[rt-step=1233272 text="0:42"]
[rt-step-group=102560 text="1:04"]
[rt-sup=202770]
[/rt-step-group]
[rt-step=1233272 text="1:28"]
[rt-step=1233272 text="1:46"]
[rt-step-group=102560 text="2:04"]
[rt-sup=202770]
[/rt-step-group]
[rt-step=1233272 text="2:31"]
[rt-half-step]
[rt-step-group=97033]
[rt-sup=16864 text="Hold your next Eclipse for Fury of Elune. Remember to pool for the Eclipse!"]
[/rt-step-group]
[/rt-half-step]
[rt-step-group=1233272 text="3:04"]
[rt-sup=202770]
[/rt-step-group]
[rt-step=1233272 text="3:26"]
[rt-step=1233272 text="3:46"]
[rt-step-group=102560 text="4:04"]
[rt-sup=202770]
[/rt-step-group]

[/rotation-timeline]
[/wrapper]
[/div]
[ul]

[li]You can hold a charge of [spell=194223] at any time to better line up with a mechanic as long as you are not sitting on 2 charges.[/li]
[li]Remember that for [symbol=wow-hero-talent-keeper-of-the-grove] [color=necrolord]Keeper of the Grove[/color], the talent [spell=434249] lets you hold any use of [spell=205636], [spell=194223]/[spell=102560] and [spell=391528] for up to 15 seconds and will reduce the cooldown depending on how long it was held. This opens up for flexibility in your cooldown windows, where you can hold on to the ability in order to use it for specific mechanics in a fight.[/li]

[/ul]
[/tab]


[tab name="Convoke the Spirits" icon=ability_ardenweald_druid]
[h3 type=bar toc=false] Convoke the Spirits[/h3]
[spell=391528] is primarily a single-target cooldown since it uses a lot of [spell=5176]s and [spell=78674]s. You want to have as many mobs afflicted by [spell=8921] as well, because [color=say]Wrath[/color]/[color=mage]Starsurge[/color] can get replaced with [spell=8921]. 
[pad]
The free [color=mage]Starsurges[/color] cast by [color=mage]Convoke the Spirits[/color] also provide 1 second value for [spell=469004], which usually adds up to about 6 or 7 seconds. 
[pad]
The spells cast by [color=mage]Convoke the Spirits[/color] work off of two separate pools of spells. One pool is filled with regular Balance spells like [spell=191034], [color=mage]Starsurge[/color], [color=say]Wrath[/color], [color=warlock]Moonfire[/color] and [spell=274283]. The other pool is filled with [color=c11]Feral/Restoration Druid[/color] spells and which ones are cast depends on your proximity to the target. On the surface, this means that using Convoke the Spirits in melee is a DPS gain, but this equals out because of the existence of [spell=429433]. [color=c11]Feral Druid[/color] spells also do very low damage so even if there is a difference it is negligible in the grand scheme of things.
[pad]
[color=white]Full Moon[/color] cast by [color=mage]Convoke the Spirits[/color] work off a stacked deck. 1 in every 5 casts will be a guaranteed Full Moon, and the deck doesn't start over until all 5 casts are done. The deck gets changed to 1 in every 2 casts instead if you are talented into 1-minute Convoke through [spell=393991].

[/tab]

sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true][/icon] Balance Druid Advanced Tips[/h2]
Balance Druid has some optimizations revolving around talents such as [spell=1239669] and [spell=393940].
[pad]
[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]


[tab name="Maximizing Uptime" icon=inv_misc_food_vendor_roastedbarlytea]

[color=c11]Balance Druid[/color] is a [b]proactive uptime spec[/b]. It has a somewhat static rotation, and even if it offers a lot of flexibility with cooldowns, it is predictable. What separates the greatest [color=c11]Balance Druid[/color] players from the average ones ultimately boils down how good you are at handling movement while also making sure you are not wasting any of your [spell=1239669] windows by casting [color=venthyr]bad spells[/color], like using [spell=8921] or [spell=93402] because you have to move and you're out of [resource=8]. 

You can read some small tips on how you can achieve better uptime below. This is not extensive and there are many other ways to do it!
[ol]

[li]Have an idea of what is going to happen later in the fight. Be aware of what mechanics are coming, and then make a decision about your positioning and how much [color=c11]Astral Power[/color] you need to have available if you get targeted by a mechanic. You can also use instant casts like [spell=78674] during your [spell=102383] animation!  [/li]
	[li][spell=1239669] can be a really good tool to help you with movement, and some fights can allow you to hold on to a charge of [color=c11]Eclipse[/color] if it means you can maintain full uptime during the mechanic, by using the instant casts from [spell=1263363]. Keep in mind that you still have to pool resources for the [color=c11]Eclipse[/color] windows!  [/li]
[li]Recognize and take advantage of situations where you can plant and cast [spell=194153] or [spell=5176]. These moments are valuable, and you want to avoid micro moving too much and getting gaps in your casts!  [/li]
[li]If you want to get an easy view of your casting uptime, the Timeline feature on the [url=https://wowanalyzer.com/]WoWAnalyzer[/url] website is pretty good. If you have a log of your character from [url=https://www.warcraftlogs.com]Warcraftlogs[/url] then you can paste the link into the website and navigate to your character. [b]You will get a warning that the spec is not supported, but if you are only using the Timeline feature you can ignore this warning[/b]. There are a few other useful tidbits on here, like a count of how much [color=c11]Astral Power[/color] you wasted during the encounter and how active you were during your cooldown windows. [/li]

[/ol]
[/tab]



[/tabs]

[pad]
 

[hr]
Our Balance Druid guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Balance Druid guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page.

[h2 toc=false]Feedback[/h2]

Thanks for reading our class guides! If you have any feedback, feel free to leave a comment in the section below, and we will reply as quickly as possible. If you'd like to talk with any of our writers directly, you can do so by joining our [url=http://discord.gg/wowhead]Discord server[/url] and finding them there!

[pad][br][pad]

[tooltip name=mushroom]Each detonation of [color=say]Wild Mushroom[/color] adds on to any existing [color=unfriendly]DoT[/color]. The usual terminology is that the [color=unfriendly]DoT[/color] [i]"ignites"[/i]. This means that using a charge while the debuff is active is neither a gain nor a loss, and doing so can be beneficial depending on heavy burst moments in AoE or if there are adds that need to die quickly. You generally do not play [color=say]Wild Mushroom[/color] in Single Target encounters.  [/tooltip]

[tooltip name=cosmos]It is a gain to use [icon name=ability_druid_starfall][/icon][color=mage]Starfall[/color] to spend Touch the Cosmos procs in Single Target because of buffs from talents like [spell=1240907] and [spell=327541]/[spell=1240262], mixed with the increased chance to proc a free [spell=78674].[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=moonfire]Even though your treants also apply Moonfire, it can be beneficial to do it yourself instead of relying on the in-game pet AI.[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=sunfire]It is generally a loss to spend GCDs on reapplying [color=unfriendly]DoTs[/color] during your damage windows, so to prevent this we ignore [color=night-fae]Pandemic[/color] and reapply it before entering our cooldown sequence. [/tooltip]


[tooltip name=MoonfireAoE]You want to start spreading Moonfire while the tank is pulling and then Sunfire when the pull is gathered.
If you find yourself ripping threat with Moonfire, try to reposition reactively so the mobs walk through the tank so they can get threat back.[/tooltip]



[tooltip name=trinket]You can macro your [icon name=inv_trinket_80_titan02a][/icon][color=warrior]On-Use Trinket[/color] together with [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color] if you want, but instant damage effects like [icon name=ability_skyreach_solar_burst][/icon][color=say]Solar Bolt[/color] will usually not benefit from the trinket buff.[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=treants][icon name=ability_druid_forceofnature][/icon][color=necrolord]Force of Nature[/color] itself does very minor damage, but provides a [color=kyrian]12%[/color] damage amp while it's active. Because of this, you always want to follow up [icon name=ability_druid_forceofnature][/icon][color=necrolord]Force of Nature[/color] by entering an [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange][/icon] [color=kyrian]Eclipse Window[/color]. Your [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color] window is your biggest damage window, while your regular [color=c11]Eclipse[/color] window is smaller. 

Because of [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color] being on a [color=kyrian]two minute[/color] recharge and [icon name=ability_druid_forceofnature][/icon][color=necrolord]Force of Nature[/color] having a [color=kyrian]60 second[/color] cooldown, you are bound to end up in situations where overlapping them is not possible.

When this happens, you have to start holding on to a charge of [icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange][/icon][color=say]Eclipse[/color] in order to overlap this cooldown instead. In a regular patchwerk fight, this happens around the [color=kyrian]three minute mark[/color]. [/tooltip]

[tooltip name=eclipse]The optimal time to press [color=c11]Eclipse[/color] depends a lot on the state of your other cooldowns. You are free to use [color=c11]Eclipse[/color] as a filler window between your bigger burst windows as long as you have [color=c11]Eclipse[/color] available for the moments where your [color=necrolord]Force of Nature[/color] and [color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color] don't overlap.[/tooltip]


[tooltip name=eclipse]The optimal time to press [color=c11]Eclipse[/color] depends a lot on the state of your other cooldowns. You are free to use [color=c11]Eclipse[/color] as a filler window between your bigger burst windows as long as you have [color=c11]Eclipse[/color] available for the moments where your [color=mage]Fury of Elune[/color] and [color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color] don't overlap.[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=starsurgeooe]You can hold on to a [color=glyph]Touch the Cosmos[/color] proc going into your cooldown windows if you don't risk munching the proc by continuing to cast [color=say]Wrath.[/color] [/tooltip]


[tooltip name=convoke]You want to cast [icon name=inv_ability_druid_convokethespirits][/icon][color=mage]Convoke the Spirits[/color] with as low amount of [color=warlock]Astral Power[/color] as possible to avoid the risk of overcapping.[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=cds]The Priority List below attempts to explain both the cooldown logic of [color=c11]Balance Druid[/color], while also separating whether you are actively in a cooldown window or not. 

It's important to understand that [color=c11]Balance Druid[/color] operates based on your available [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange][/icon] [color=kyrian]Eclipse Windows[/color] and how those windows interact with the signature ability for your chosen Hero Tree.

The effect of [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color] acts as a more powerful version of your regular [icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange][/icon][color=c11]Eclipse[/color] cooldown, providing the benefit of both [icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange][/icon][color=say]Solar Eclipse[/color] and [icon name=ability_druid_eclipse][/icon][color=warlock]Lunar Eclipse[/color].  

Pressing [icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange][/icon][color=c11]Eclipse[/color] during the effect of your [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color] does not work, and pressing [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color] during your [icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange][/icon][color=c11]Eclipse[/color] will remove the existing buff and begin a fresh one.

Playing [color=necrolord]Keeper of the Grove[/color] changes your [icon name=ability_druid_forceofnature][/icon][color=necrolord]Force of Nature[/color] spell to provide a damage bonus during it's effect. Because of this, we want to align it with [b][color=venthyr]EITHER[/color][/b] [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color] or [icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange][/icon][color=c11]Eclipse[/color], depending on which ones are available to you.[/tooltip]
[tooltip name=cooldownline]This section aims to explain [b]both[/b] the logic [b]and[/b] the sequence in which you want to use your cooldowns. [/tooltip]



[tooltip name=eccds]The Priority List below attempts to explain both the cooldown logic of [color=c11]Balance Druid[/color], while also separating whether you are actively in a cooldown window or not. 

It's important to understand that [color=c11]Balance Druid[/color] operates based on your available [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange][/icon] [color=kyrian]Eclipse Windows[/color] and how those windows interact with the signature ability for your chosen Hero Tree.

The effect of [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color] acts as a more powerful version of your regular [icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange][/icon][color=c11]Eclipse[/color] cooldown, providing the benefit of both [icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange][/icon][color=say]Solar Eclipse[/color] and [icon name=ability_druid_eclipse][/icon][color=warlock]Lunar Eclipse[/color].  

Pressing [icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange][/icon][color=c11]Eclipse[/color] during the effect of your [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color] does not work, and pressing [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color] during your [icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange][/icon][color=c11]Eclipse[/color] will remove the existing buff and begin a fresh one.

When you're playing [symbol=wow-hero-talent-elunes-chosen] [color=c9]Elune's Chosen[/color], your [icon name=ability_druid_dreamstate][/icon][color=mage]Fury of Elune[/color] is turned into a damage cooldown. The way you approach this spell is similar to [color=necrolor]Keeper of the Grove[/color], where you want to align it with [b][color=venthyr]EITHER[/color][/b] [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color] or [icon name=ability_druid_eclipse][/icon][color=c11]Eclipse[/color], depending on which ones are available to you. [/tooltip]

[tooltip name=foeec]The value in [icon name=ability_druid_dreamstate][/icon][color=mage]Fury of Elune[/color] lies in providing you with uptime on [spell=429532] as well as providing you with a steady flow of [resource=8]. Because of this, we want to use it on the GCD [b]before[/b] using our bigger cooldowns in [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color] or [icon name=ability_druid_eclipse][/icon][color=c11]Eclipse[/color] [/tooltip]

[tooltip name=eclipse2]The line above takes priority, meaning this line is only applicable for [icon name=ability_druid_forceofnature][/icon][color=necrolord]Force of Nature[/color] casts that cannot overlap with [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color]/[icon name=spell_druid_incarnation][/icon][color=mage]Incarnation[/color]. In a normal patchwerk fight this would happen around the [color=kyrian]three minute mark[/color].[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=eclipse3]The line above takes priority, meaning this line is only applicable for [icon name=ability_druid_dreamstate][/icon][color=mage]Fury of Elune[/color] casts that cannot overlap with [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color]/[icon name=spell_druid_incarnation][/icon][color=mage]Incarnation[/color]. In a normal patchwerk fight this would happen around the [color=kyrian]three minute mark[/color].[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=EclipseInc]Since [icon name=spell_druid_incarnation][/icon][color=mage]Incarnation: Chosen of Elune[/color] lasts for [color=kyrian]20[/color] seconds, it is optimal to use a charge of [icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange][/icon][color=say]Eclipse[/color] to get the cooldown rolling as soon as possible. This usually only applies for the very start of combat![/tooltip]

[tooltip name=EclipseInc2]Since [icon name=spell_nature_natureguardian][/icon][color=mage]Celestial Alignment[/color] lasts for [color=kyrian]15[/color] seconds, you may want to use a charge of [icon name=ability_druid_eclipseorange][/icon][color=say]Eclipse[/color] to get the cooldown rolling as soon as possible. This usually only applies for the very start of combat![/tooltip]

This usually only applies for the very start of combat![/tooltip]

[tooltip name=eclipseaoe]In a Mythic+ pull you can press this while you're spreading Moonfire! [/tooltip]

[/tooltip]
